prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1287; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a low-speed collision while backing out of a space in a parking lot and stated that a left shoulder injury occurred at the time. The claim was opened and the claimant confirmed representation by counsel, with all further contact to go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Verified that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the reported loss. No issues with the policy were found.

Entry 3: The police report and the statements of the responding officers confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. Photos from the scene were requested and received.

Entry 4: Reviewed the scene photographs, which confirm some of the details described in the claimant's account. No independent witnesses have been identified to date.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed. The damage is mostly in line with the impact described by the claimant. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or records.

Entry 6: Medical records show the reported shoulder injury fits the kind and force of the crash. No prior injury or treatment to the same body area is known from available records.

Entry 7: Counsel's demand package received and reviewed. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved, consistent with the records provided.

Entry 8: The claimant later provided additional small details about the sequence of events, but the core account has remained the same across all statements taken to date.

Entry 9: Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the policy coverage began. Dates of loss and policy inception were cross-checked and align.

Entry 10: File reviewed with the claim supervisor. The claim remains open pending final medical updates from the treating provider and any further correspondence from counsel.
